# Juneau

React component library for building AI chat interfaces. Streaming-first, adapter-based, fully themeable. No AI API calls — the consumer owns the network layer via an adapter.

## Architecture

Two providers wrap the app:
- `JuneauProvider` — theme tokens + UI labels (i18n)
- `AiChatProvider` — holds conversation state (messages, input, loading), accepts the adapter

`AiSidebar` reads state from `AiChatProvider` via context. Conversation persists across page navigation. Pages update AI context per-route via `setContext()`.

## Providers

### JuneauProvider
Props: `theme?: JuneauTheme`, `labels?: Partial<JuneauLabels>`, `className?`, `style?`
Provides CSS token overrides and UI string overrides to all Juneau components in the subtree.

### AiChatProvider
Props: `adapter: AiBackendAdapter`, `context?: Record<string, unknown>`, `onProposalConfirm?`, `onProposalCancel?`, `children`
Holds shared useAiChat state. Wrap once at app/layout root. One provider = one persistent conversation.
Props: `adapter`, `context?`, `onProposalConfirm?`, `onProposalCancel?`, `initialMessages?`, `historyLimit?`, `onMessagesChange?` — the three history props are forwarded to the internal useAiChat.

## Hooks

### useAiChatContext()
Returns all useAiChat fields plus `setContext(ctx)`. Must be inside AiChatProvider — throws outside one.
Use `setContext()` on each page to pass current page, available tools, entity IDs, etc. to the adapter.
`setContext(obj)` REPLACES the whole context; `setContext(prev => ({ ...prev, key: v }))` merges (updater form).
Safe escape hatch outside a guaranteed provider: `useContext(AiChatContext)` returns `AiChatContextValue | null` — `AiChatContext` is exported from the main barrel.

### useAiChat(options)
Low-level hook for custom UIs. Options: `adapter`, `context?`, `onProposalConfirm?`, `onProposalCancel?`, `initialMessages?` (restored conversation), `historyLimit?` (max messages sent to adapter per request — token saving, rendering never trimmed), `onMessagesChange?` (fires when conversation settles — stream done, proposal resolved, reset; never per token — use to persist)
Returns: `messages`, `input`, `setInput`, `sendMessage`, `sendMessageWithText`, `sendGreeting`, `stop`, `isLoading`, `isConnecting`, `error`, `reset(nextMessages?)` (pass messages to switch to another stored chat), `confirmProposal`, `cancelProposal`
`confirmProposal`/`cancelProposal` also mark the proposal `resolved` in message state — the card renders disabled with a badge.

## Components

### AiSidebar
Fixed-position overlay panel, bottom-right, reads from AiChatProvider.
Props: `title?`, `icon?`, `actions?`, `sendIcon?`, `height?` (default: '60vh'), `onReset?`, `renderPart?`, `onEntityClick?`, `aboveInput?`, `className?`, `style?`
Has minimize/restore button. Minimized = compact header bar at bottom-right. Animated transition.

### AiChat
Headless chat body (message list + input + error). Requires explicit props from useAiChat.
Use when embedding chat in a custom layout instead of using AiSidebar. Also accepts `renderPart?` and `onEntityClick?`.
`aboveInput?: ReactNode` renders consumer content between the message list / error and the input, wrapped in `[data-juneau="above-input"][data-juneau-above-input]`. Omitted or null = nothing rendered, no wrapper. AiSidebar forwards the same prop (hidden while minimized).

`AiChat` `centerInputWhenEmpty?: boolean` + `belowInput?: ReactNode`: with no messages, empty state + input + `belowInput` stack centred in `[data-juneau="chat-start"]` (`belowInput` in `[data-juneau="below-input"]`); the first message restores the default layout.

### renderPart — custom part renderer escape hatch
`RenderPartFn = (part: AiMessagePart) => ReactNode | null | undefined`
Called before the built-in renderers for every part. Non-nullish return wins (can override built-ins too); null/undefined falls through. Receives the raw part with no narrowing — consumer owns type assertions:

```tsx
<AiSidebar renderPart={part => {
  if (part.type === 'invoice-card') return <InvoiceCard part={part as InvoiceCardPart} />;
  return null; // fall through to built-ins
}} />
```

Threaded down: AiSidebar/AiChat → AiMessageList → AiMessageBubble → AiMessagePartRenderer.

### AiChatHeader
Props: `title?`, `icon?`, `onMinimize?`, `isMinimized?`

### AiInput
Props: `value`, `onChange`, `onSend`, `onStop?`, `isLoading`, `placeholder?`, `actions?`, `sendIcon?`

### AiMessageList
Props: `messages`, `isLoading`, `isConnecting`, `onProposalConfirm`, `onProposalCancel`, `onEntityClick?`, `assistantIcon?`

### AiMessageBubble
Props: `message`, `onProposalConfirm`, `onProposalCancel`, `onEntityClick?`, `assistantIcon?`

### AiMessagePartRenderer
Dispatches AiMessagePart to the correct renderer. Part types: text, table, entity, entity-list, proposal, activity, error.

### AiActivityPart
Renders an activity item (running/done/failed). Subtle UI — not a main response, shows AI progress.
Running state has a pulsing pink dot. Done = green dot. Failed = red dot.

### AiTablePart
Renders a data table from columns + rows.

### AiEntityCard
Renders a structured entity (`{ id?, title, subtitle?, fields?, payload? }`) as a card with labelled field rows. Fields can render as badges (`success | warning | danger | neutral`). Becomes a clickable `<button>` when `onEntityClick?(entity, entityType?)` is provided — use it to navigate to the record. `entity.payload` is opaque, never rendered.

### AiEntityListPart
Renders `entities: AiEntity[]` as stacked AiEntityCards with an optional `title` heading. Same `onEntityClick` behaviour.

### AiProposalCard
Renders a confirm/cancel card. Calls onProposalConfirm(id, payload) or onProposalCancel(id).
If `proposal.resolved` is set (`'confirmed' | 'cancelled' | 'expired'`), buttons are replaced by a status badge and the card dims.

### AiChatHistoryList
Renders a list of stored chats. Props: `chats: AiChatSummary[]`, `onSelect(chatId)`, `activeChatId?`, `onDelete?(chatId)`.
`AiChatSummary = { id, title, createdAt: Date, updatedAt: Date }`. Consumer owns storage and selection.

### AiTypingIndicator
Shows animated dots while streaming or connecting.

### AiError
Dismissable error banner.

## Stream event types

```
AiStreamEvent =
  | { type: 'text'; text: string }
  | { type: 'part'; part: AiMessagePart }
  | { type: 'done' }
  | { type: 'error'; message: string }
```

## Message part types

```
AiMessagePart =
  | { type: 'text'; text: string }
  | { type: 'table'; columns: string[]; rows: Record<string, unknown>[] }
  | { type: 'entity'; entity: AiEntity; entityType?: string }
  | { type: 'entity-list'; entities: AiEntity[]; title?: string; entityType?: string }
  | { type: 'proposal'; proposal: AiProposal }
  | { type: 'activity'; id?: string; title: string; description?: string; status: 'running' | 'done' | 'failed'; metadata?: Record<string, unknown> }
  | { type: 'error'; message: string }
  | AiCustomPart   // { type: string; [key: string]: unknown } — consumer-defined, rendered via renderPart

AiEntity = { id?: string; title: string; subtitle?: string; fields?: AiEntityField[]; payload?: unknown }
AiEntityField = { label: string; value: string; badge?: 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'neutral' }
```

Custom parts (any `type` string not matching a built-in) flow through the wire protocol and message state untouched. Render them via the `renderPart` prop on `AiSidebar` / `AiChat`. Juneau applies no validation or narrowing — the consumer owns all type assertions. Unhandled custom parts show a dashed warning outline in dev, render nothing in production.

Activity parts with a stable `id` update in-place when a new part with the same `id` arrives. Without `id`, they append as a timeline.

## Adapter interface

```ts
interface AiBackendAdapter {
  sendMessage(input: AiAdapterInput): AsyncIterable<AiStreamEvent>;
}

type AiAdapterInput = {
  messages: AiMessage[];
  context?: Record<string, unknown>;
};
```

## Built-in adapters

- `createSseAdapter(url, options?)` — SSE streaming. Default parser understands Juneau wire protocol first, falls back to OpenAI format (`choices[0].delta.content`). Options: `method`, `headers`, `getHeaders`, `getBody`, `credentials`, `parseEvent`.
- `createFetchStreamAdapter(url, options?)` — raw chunked HTTP / NDJSON. Default parser understands Juneau wire protocol; falls back to treating unknown chunks as plain text. Options: `method`, `headers`, `getHeaders`, `getBody`, `credentials`, `parseChunk`.
- `mockAdapter` — dev-only, keyword-triggered scenarios: table, entity, proposal, activity, help, error.

Both adapters accept `credentials?: RequestCredentials` for cross-origin cookie auth (`'include'`).

## Chat history helpers

Juneau is storage-agnostic — the consumer persists chats, Juneau defines the contract and renders restored conversations (all rich parts re-render from plain data, no reconstruction needed).

- `serializeForStorage(messages)` → `AiSerializedMessage[]` — JSON-safe: dates → ISO strings, unresolved proposals marked `resolved: 'expired'` (restored cards render disabled, never fire stale callbacks), `running` activity parts dropped.
- `deserializeMessages(stored)` → `AiMessage[]` — revives `createdAt` dates. Feed to `initialMessages` or `reset()`.
- `trimHistory(messages, limit)` — keeps the most recent `limit` messages; never starts on an assistant turn (alternation stays valid). Used internally by `historyLimit`.
- `trimChats(chats, limit)` — returns the `limit` most recently updated `AiChatSummary[]`, sorted newest first. Enforce overall chats limit by deleting the rest from storage.

## Juneau wire protocol

Standard JSON format Juneau-compatible backends should stream. Both adapters parse this automatically — no custom parser needed.

Each SSE `data:` line or NDJSON line must be one of:

```
{ "type": "text", "text": "string" }

{ "type": "activity", "id"?: "string", "title": "string", "description"?: "string", "status": "running" | "done" | "failed", "metadata"?: {} }

{ "type": "part", "part": { "type": "table", ... } | { "type": "entity", ... } | { "type": "entity-list", ... } | { "type": "proposal", ... } }

{ "type": "done" }

{ "type": "error", "message": "string" }
```

Activity `id` behaviour: same `id` → update in-place (running → done). No `id` → append as timeline row.
Activity `metadata`: opaque, not rendered by Juneau. Use for internal data (tool name, duration, skill ID).

Exported wire types: `JuneauWireEvent`, `JuneauWireText`, `JuneauWireActivity`, `JuneauWirePart`, `JuneauWireDone`, `JuneauWireError`.
Shared parser utility: `parseJuneauWire(raw: string): AiStreamEvent[]` — used internally by both adapters, not exported.

## Server utilities — `juneau/server`

Node-only helpers for Juneau-compatible backends. Import from the `/server` subpath (keeps zod out of the browser bundle):

```ts
import { toSdkMessages, createSkillSet, buildSkillIndex, selectSkills, selectSkillsById, streamToWire, withToolRecovery, withSkillDispatch } from 'juneau/server';
```

### toSdkMessages(messages: AiMessage[]): CoreMessage[]
Converts Juneau message history to ai-sdk's CoreMessage format. Extracts text parts, replaces activity-only assistant messages with an empty-text turn, injects placeholder assistant turns between consecutive user messages, and filters empty turns.

### createSkillSet(skills, options?) → SkillSet
Wraps skill definitions into ai-sdk tool definitions with a built-in activity event buffer. Each tool call automatically emits `running`, `done`, and `failed` Juneau wire SSE strings into the buffer.

SkillDefinition fields: `title`, `description`, `id` (numeric, required — chosen by the consumer, must be unique across the skill map; createSkillSet throws at startup on duplicates), `instructions?` (workflow text, lazily loaded via selectSkills/selectSkillsById), `readOnly?` (default true), `requiresConfirmation?` (default false), `tools?` (skill composition — validated at startup, throws on unknown reference), `input` (ZodType), `labels.running`, `labels.done`, `labels.failed?`, `execute(input, { emit })`.

SkillSet also exposes `skills` (original definitions), `skillsById` (Map&lt;number, SkillDefinition&gt; — lookup by numeric ID), `calledSkillNames` (skills the model called during phase 1, deduplicated, in call order), and `calledSkillIds` (same, but as numeric IDs — use with selectSkillsById).

### buildSkillIndex(skillSet) → string
Compact one-liner-per-skill index for the system prompt: `[1] invoiceSearch (read): Find invoices…` / `[2] invoiceApprove (write, requires confirmation): …`. Numeric ID is included so the model can request skills by ID — avoids string comparisons on the backend. Registry-driven — adding a skill updates the index automatically.

### selectSkills(skillSet, skillNames) → string
Concatenated `instructions` for the given skill names (typically `skillSet.calledSkillNames` after phase 1). Lazy loading: full workflow instructions enter the prompt only for skills the model actually used. Unknown names and skills without instructions are skipped; returns `''` when nothing matches.

### selectSkillsById(skillSet, skillIds) → string
Same as selectSkills but resolves by numeric ID — use with `skillSet.calledSkillIds` to avoid string comparisons entirely. Unknown IDs and skills without instructions are skipped; returns `''` when nothing matches.

`execute` receives a `SkillExecuteContext` as second argument: `emit(part)` pushes a custom part wire event (`{ type: 'part', part }`) into the same buffer as activities — drained by `streamToWire` at the same points. Available synchronously at any point during execution. Use to stream rich widgets (e.g. invoice cards) alongside the tool result:

```ts
execute: async ({ query }, { emit }) => {
  const inv = await db.findInvoice(query);
  emit({ type: 'invoice-card', invoiceNumber: inv.number, amount: inv.total });
  return { found: 1, invoice: inv }; // returned to model as tool result
}
```

SkillSet fields: `tools` (pass to streamText), `drainActivities()` (returns and clears buffered SSE strings), `hadFailure`, `failureContext`.

SkillSetOptions: `language?` (default: `'en'`) — selects which label variant to use. `debug?` (default: `false`) — emit `console.debug` logs per skill execution.

### streamToWire(fullStream, skillSet?, options?) → AsyncIterable\<string\>
Converts ai-sdk `fullStream` to Juneau wire SSE strings. Handles all ai-sdk v7 text chunk types (`text-delta` and `text`, with `textDelta` v6 fallback). Drains `skillSet.drainActivities()` before each text chunk and once after the loop. Emits `done` event at the end. `options.debug` logs every chunk received.

### withSkillDispatch(options) → AsyncIterable\<string\>
Deliberate 2-phase skill dispatch pattern — the clean alternative to mashing all skill instructions into one big system prompt.

Phase 1: stream with `buildSkillIndex` as the system prompt and thin tool definitions. The model picks a skill by calling a tool — `calledSkillIds` is populated as tools fire.
Phase 2: always runs when at least one skill was called. Receives the full workflow instructions for the called skills (`selectSkillsById`) and the complete phase 1 message history (user + tool-call + tool-result turns). The model is called again without tools so it reads the instructions and produces a text response.
If no skill was called in phase 1 (model answered directly), phase 1 text is emitted as-is and the stream ends cleanly.
Phase 2 errors are emitted as wire `error` events, never swallowed.

Options: `phase1: () => ToolRecoveryStreamResult`, `phase2: (instructions: string, messages: unknown[]) => { fullStream }`, `skillSet`, `onFinish?`, `debug?`.

```ts
for await (const chunk of withSkillDispatch({
  phase1: () => streamText({ model, system: buildSkillIndex(skillSet), messages: sdkMessages, tools: skillSet.tools, maxSteps: 1 }),
  phase2: (instructions, history) => streamText({ model, system: instructions, messages: history }),
  skillSet,
})) {
  res.write(chunk);
}
```

### withToolRecovery(options) → AsyncIterable\<string\>
Multi-phase streaming pattern for Gemini 2.5 Flash tool call recovery. Phase 1 streams with tools. If a tool failed and no text was produced, phase 2 calls the model without tools, injecting `failureContext` as an assistant message to force a text response. If the tool succeeded but no text was produced (Gemini treats the tool call as its complete response — confirmed chunk sequence: tool-call → tool-result → finish-step → finish, no text-delta), optional phase 3 receives the full phase 1 message history (resolved from the ai-sdk result's `messages` promise — resolves to ALL turns incl. tool-call + tool-result after the stream is consumed; `response.messages` is fallback only, may miss tool-result turns which Gemini rejects) and calls the model again without tools to summarise the result. Without `phase3`, emits `done` cleanly. Phase 2/3 errors are emitted as wire `error` events, never swallowed. `debug` logs the resolved phase 3 message array and warns when no tool-result turn is present.

Options: `phase1: () => ToolRecoveryStreamResult` (pass the streamText result directly — `fullStream` + `messages`), `phase2: (failureContext) => { fullStream }`, `phase3?: (messages) => { fullStream }`, `skillSet`, `debug?`.

```ts
for await (const chunk of withToolRecovery({
  phase1: () => streamText({ model, system, messages: sdkMessages, tools: skillSet.tools, maxSteps: 2 }),
  phase2: (ctx) => streamText({ model, system, messages: [...sdkMessages, { role: 'assistant', content: ctx }] }),
  phase3: (fullMessages) => streamText({ model, system, messages: fullMessages }),
  skillSet,
})) {
  res.write(chunk);
}
```

---

## Typical integration pattern

```tsx
// main.tsx
<JuneauProvider labels={juneauCs}>
  <AiChatProvider
    adapter={createSseAdapter('/api/chat')}
    onProposalConfirm={(id, payload) => handleAction(id, payload)}
  >
    <App />
  </AiChatProvider>
</JuneauProvider>

// Layout or any persistent shell
<AiSidebar />

// Any page — tell AI where the user is
const { setContext } = useAiChatContext();
useEffect(() => {
  setContext({ page: 'invoices', tools: ['search', 'export'], role: 'admin' });
}, []);
```

## Exports

Types: `AiMessage`, `AiMessageRole`, `AiMessagePart`, `AiCustomPart`, `AiTextPart`, `AiTablePartType`, `AiProposalPart`, `AiProposal`, `AiActivityPartType`, `AiActivityStatus`, `AiErrorPart`, `AiBackendAdapter`, `AiAdapterInput`, `AiStreamEvent`, `AiStreamTextEvent`, `AiStreamPartEvent`, `AiStreamDoneEvent`, `AiStreamErrorEvent`, `JuneauWireEvent`, `JuneauWireText`, `JuneauWireActivity`, `JuneauWirePart`, `JuneauWireDone`, `JuneauWireError`, `JuneauTheme`, `JuneauLabels`, `AiInputAction`, `RenderPartFn`, `UseAiChatOptions`, `UseAiChatReturn`, `AiChatContextValue`

Components now exported: `AiSidebar`, `AiChat`, `AiMessageList`, `AiMessageBubble`, `AiInput`, `AiTypingIndicator`, `AiError`, `AiMessagePartRenderer`, `AiTablePart`, `AiProposalCard`, `AiActivityPart`

Utilities: `consumeStream`, `delay`, `getMessageText`

Locales: `juneauEn`, `juneauCs`
